To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dry mass of the polytine chromosomes is not uniform throughout, but varies from region to region; (2) the dry mass increases during development; (3) the dry mass is heterogeneous in the bands and in the interbands; (4) the nucleolus is a heterogeneous structure; (5) the nucleolos, bands and interbands contain protein; (6) the nucleoloi, bands and interband regions contain DNA and RNA;

(1) the refractive index of the polytine chromosomes in Drosophila is about 1.38; (2) the dry mass concentration of the polytines is about 1 mg/ml; and (3) the polytine bands contain 5 % RNA, 6 % DNA, and 89 % protein, whereas the interbands contain 1 % RNA, 1 % DNA, and about 98 % protein.

the dry mass concentration and the refractive index of the band and interbands of Drosophilla polytene chromosomes change during larval development and that the dry mass of the nucleoplasm, nucleoli, bands and interbands can be altered in vitro by enzymes and in vivo by cold shock.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantitative determination of the cytophysics of polytene nuclei.
the quantitative determination of the cytophysics of polytene chromosome components.
the physical and chemical properties of the polytenized chromosomal regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polytene chromosome is a complex, dynamic, heterogeneous structure.
the band and interbands are heterogeneous, and the interbands are not simply the DNA-free areas of bands.
the band and interbands are composed of protein, RNA, and DNA, with protein predominating in the bands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bands and interband are composed of protein, RNA, and DNA in a ratio of about 70:25:5.

1) the band and interbands are heterogeneous, 2) the bands and interband contain about the same amount of protein, 3) the nucleolus and nucleoplasm contain more than 50% of the dry mass of the nucleus, 4) the nucleololus contains more protein than RNA, and 5) the bands are rich in RNA
